name: Inositol
lead: Inositol is a sugar alcohol with the formula C6H12O6 that is a component of cell structures and acts as a signaling molecule in eukaryotic cells; myo-inositol is the most abundant form, and D-chiro-inositol is another isomer sold as a supplement [1]. It is found in fruit (oranges and cantaloupe especially), beans, nuts and grains, and is also made in the body, mainly in the kidneys [1].

People take it for looks mainly through hormone and skin pathways. Its best-studied supplement use is in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a condition whose visible features include acne, excess facial and body hair and irregular cycles; Wikipedia describes reported benefits of inositol for insulin sensitivity, hyperandrogenism and cycle regularity [1][13]. The chain proposed by proponents is better insulin signaling, then lower androgen activity, then fewer androgen-driven skin and hair changes. A 2023 meta-analysis of 26 randomized trials reported larger reductions in free and total testosterone with inositol than with placebo [15].

In looksmaxxing communities it is mentioned in sleep and calming stacks, and in forum claims about testosterone and jaw growth. Those claims concern healthy men and growth, and no published trial tests inositol for sleep, jaw development or facial appearance in that setting [11][12].

paras: Inositol exists as several stereoisomers, with myo-inositol the most abundant; once called vitamin B8, it lost that classification because the body makes it [1]. In biochemistry and medicine the word usually means myo-inositol. It is a six-carbon ring with a hydroxyl group on each carbon, a white crystalline powder with about half the sweetness of sucrose [1].

Supplements are sold as myo-inositol alone, D-chiro-inositol alone, or mixtures. Wikipedia notes that the plasma ratio of myo- to D-chiro-inositol in healthy people is roughly 40:1 and that this ratio is the one most often studied in combination products [1]. A randomized comparison of ratios in PCOS patients examined whether the 40:1 mixture restored ovulation better than other ratios [18].

Humans make myo-inositol from glucose 6-phosphate in two enzyme steps, with the kidneys producing most of it, on the order of 2 grams per day; the brain holds the highest concentration, and most mammalian cells keep it at many times the level outside the cell [1]. An insulin-dependent enzyme converts a small fraction to D-chiro-inositol, and Wikipedia reports that insulin resistance reduces D-chiro-inositol in muscle, fat and liver [1].

Foods such as oranges and cantaloupe contain free myo-inositol, while beans, nuts and grains hold much of it as phytic acid (inositol hexaphosphate), the main phosphorus store in seeds and bran. Phytic acid binds calcium, magnesium, iron and zinc, and non-ruminants lack the enzyme to use it readily; inositol in lecithin is well absorbed [1]. Most commercial myo-inositol is made from corn or rice bran phytate, with China and Japan the main producers as of 2021 [1].

Inositol phosphates are central to cell signaling: inositol trisphosphate acts as a second messenger that releases intracellular calcium, work described in highly cited 1984 and 1993 papers [2][3]. Phosphatidylinositol lipids and glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchors are structural parts of cell membranes, and inositol phosphate glycans form in response to insulin and help mediate its glucose effects [1].

A 2023 narrative review in Nutrients describes myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol as modulators of ovarian steroidogenesis, the pathway by which the ovary makes hormones including androgens and estrogens [17]. Wikipedia states that D-chiro-inositol reduces conversion of testosterone to estrogen, which it presents as raising testosterone in the PCOS context [1]; this is the source of the forum argument that the two isomers move testosterone in opposite directions.

For appearance, interest centers on PCOS-related features. PCOS can include acne, hirsutism (excess terminal hair) and irregular cycles, and standard management described by Wikipedia includes contraceptive pills, metformin, laser hair removal and ordinary acne treatments; it adds that metformin is recommended over inositol supplements for hirsutism and abdominal fat [13]. A randomized comparative study titled Inositol and acne examined the supplement in acne [16].

Some men's forums raise inositol in a different frame, as a calming ingredient in sleep stacks or as something that shifts testosterone or growth-related hormones [11][12]. These are community claims rather than trial endpoints.

Wikipedia lists PCOS as the main clinical use, along with studies in metabolic disease where supplementation reduced triglycerides and LDL cholesterol, a role in thyroid hormone synthesis, and combination with folic acid in neural tube defect prevention work; for trichotillomania, high doses have been explored without definitive evidence of effectiveness [1].

Registered trials focus on PCOS, infertility and gestational diabetes, testing myo-inositol alone, D-chiro-inositol, or a combination mixture [4][5][6][7][8]. A registered trial in children with bipolar disorder and anxiety was withdrawn [9].

A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis in Reproductive Biology and Endocrinology pooled 26 randomized trials (1,691 patients) comparing inositols with placebo or metformin in PCOS. It reported that inositol users were 1.79 times as likely as placebo users to have a regular cycle, that the effect was non-inferior to metformin for that outcome, and that inositols produced larger reductions in BMI, free and total testosterone, androstenedione, glucose and insulin area under the curve, with higher sex hormone-binding globulin [15].

A systematic review and meta-analysis prepared to inform the 2023 international PCOS guideline covered 30 trials (2,230 participants) and described benefits of myo-inositol or D-chiro-inositol for some metabolic measures and potential benefits of D-chiro-inositol for ovulation, with no effect on other outcomes; it also reported that metformin may improve waist-hip ratio and hirsutism compared with inositol, with no clear difference in reproductive outcomes [14]. Individual randomized trials have compared myo-inositol with metformin [20], myo-inositol with D-chiro-inositol [19], and metformin plus inositols versus metformin alone [21]. No trial has measured inositol for sleep, jaw growth or other appearance outcomes in healthy people.

Wikipedia reports very low toxicity for myo-inositol (oral rat LD50 10,000 mg/kg) but does not discuss human side effects [1]. The 2023 PCOS meta-analysis title describes inositol as a safe treatment in that population [15]. Labels for combination products advise pregnant or breastfeeding people to ask a health professional [10].

Johannes Joseph Scherer first isolated inositol from muscle extracts in 1850; the prefix myo- refers to muscle [1]. In 1936 Edward Bartow of the University of Iowa described extracting it from corn phytate waste, and inositol nitrate was later explored as a stabler alternative to nitroglycerin [1]. Second-messenger work on inositol trisphosphate in the 1980s made inositol phosphates a major topic in cell biology [3]. Supplement research in PCOS expanded through the 2010s and 2020s, as shown by registered trials from 2012 onward [4][6].

Inositol is sold over the counter as a powder or capsule and appears in energy drinks and women's health supplements [1]. Wikipedia also notes it is used as a cutting agent for illicit drugs, an industrial fact unrelated to supplement use [1]. In looksmaxxing spaces, threads present it either as a hormone-supporting supplement or as something that could harm growth, with posters citing single studies or mechanisms [11][12].

timeline.event: Scherer isolates inositol from muscle extracts [1].
Bartow describes extracting inositol from waste corn phytate [1].
Inositol trisphosphate is described as a second messenger in cell signaling [3].

Registered trial of myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol in gestational diabetes begins [4].

Meta-analysis of 26 randomized trials in PCOS published [15]; systematic review for the international PCOS guideline update follows in 2024 [14].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org inositol is discussed both as a hormone-supporting supplement and, in a separate thread, as something said to harm growth [11][12].

claims.claim: D-chiro-inositol raises testosterone and myo-inositol helps glucose and lipids
claims.believers: A forum post says one study found D-chiro-inositol improved testosterone and androstenedione in older hypogonadal men, and that myo-inositol improves blood glucose and lipids [11].
claims.experts: Wikipedia says supplementation may lower triglycerides and LDL cholesterol in metabolic disease [1]; no study tests testosterone effects in healthy men.

claims.claim: Myo-inositol lowers androgens and could stunt mandibular growth
claims.believers: A forum thread argues myo-inositol reduces testosterone and DHT and speeds growth-plate closure, so it would hamper jaw development [12].
claims.experts: No published human study has examined inositol and jaw growth or growth-plate closure.

claims.claim: Inositol calms the nervous system and helps sleep
claims.believers: Community members list inositol with other calming supplements in sleep and anxiety stacks, citing personal experience.
claims.experts: Wikipedia mentions trichotillomania exploration without definitive evidence, and a registered pediatric anxiety trial was withdrawn [1][9]; no trial tests sleep outcomes.

claims.claim: Inositol clears androgen-related acne and hirsutism
claims.believers: Supplement users with PCOS report skin and cycle improvements, and brands market it for hormonal balance.
claims.experts: A 2023 meta-analysis found larger drops in free and total testosterone than placebo [15], while a guideline-oriented review reported metformin may improve hirsutism more than inositol [14].

claims.claim: Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol have opposite effects on testosterone
claims.believers: The forum view is that D-chiro-inositol lifts androgens while myo-inositol lowers them, so the isomer chosen matters [11][12].
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes D-chiro-inositol as reducing testosterone-to-estrogen conversion [1]; a narrative review frames both isomers as modulators of ovarian steroidogenesis [17]. Trials have been in women with PCOS.

claims.claim: Inositol is an alternative to metformin for insulin resistance
claims.believers: PCOS supplement users prefer it because metformin can cause stomach side effects.
claims.experts: The 2023 meta-analysis found inositols non-inferior to metformin for cycle regularity [15]; the guideline review found metformin may be better for waist-hip ratio and hirsutism [14].

card.summary: A sugar-alcohol supplement studied mainly for PCOS; its looksmaxxing sleep and growth claims are untested.
card.note: Human research centers on PCOS and pregnancy-related conditions, not appearance.

quick.overview:
Inositol is a naturally occurring sugar alcohol found in fruit, grains and the body. Supplements are used mainly for PCOS, and some looksmaxxers add it to calming or sleep stacks.
Forum posts also make claims about testosterone and jaw growth that no study has tested.
quick.mechanism: It forms part of cell signaling molecules such as inositol trisphosphate, which regulate intracellular calcium and insulin signaling.
quick.risks: Toxicity appears very low in animal data, but human side-effect information is limited; pregnant and breastfeeding people are advised to consult a professional.

chain: Supports insulin signaling and ovarian steroid metabolism
Lower androgen markers in PCOS trials
Possible fewer androgen-related acne and hair-growth features
angle.text: In PCOS, inositol is taken to improve insulin sensitivity and androgen markers, which proponents link to clearer skin and more regular cycles. Looksmaxxing forums also discuss it as a calming or sleep-stack ingredient.
